newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:
Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said Commissioner Marcelino Oreja would hold a news conference on exclusive transmission of sports events at 1215/1115 GMT on Wednesday.
Vale de Almeida also said Commission President Jacques Santer and Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker would meet the press in the Breydel's VIP corner at 1430/1330 GMT on Wednesday.

Spokeswoman Sophie Petzel said there would be an informal Justice and Home Affairs Council on Wednesday and Thursday in Noordwijk, Netherlands. She said the main focus of discussions would be the fight against organised crime, third pillar issues and the situation of the inter-governmental conference (IGC).
In answer to a question Petzell said the question of the European Observatory on Racism and Xenophobia was not formally scheduled on the informal meeting's agenda.
Spokesman Jochen Kubosch said the Court of Justice had rejected two actions against Commission regulations on the banana market.

Kubosch also said the Advocate General's opinion on the European Parliament and France's dispute over the annulment of the European Parliament determination laying down the calendar for 1996 would not be available for a few days.
In answer to a question, spokesman Josep Coll i Carbo said Indonesia had rejected direct Commission aid to East Timor but had not rejected the principle of aid if the discussions passed via Jakarta.
Spokesman Peter Guilford's conclusions on the EU-Japan agreement on liquor tax dispute were "if you push long and hard, you get to the point".
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/82: President Constantinescu visits the European Commission.
- IP/97/83: Commission proposes exceptionnal financial assistance to Armenia, Georgia and Tajikistan.
- IP/97/84: EU and Japan agree outcome on liquor tax dispute.
